flashcard_questions.a: The belief in the absolute oneness of Allah.
Associating partners with Allah, or giving God-like qualities to anything else.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do Muslims avoid making images of Allah and Muhammad?
flashcard_questions.a: Because depicting them risks Shirk, so Islamic art uses geometry and calligraphy.

flashcard_questions.q: Which surah is the key Qur’anic text on the oneness of God?
What does the name Al-Qadir say about Allah?
flashcard_questions.a: That He is omnipotent — all-powerful and able to do anything.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the name Ar-Rahim say about Allah?
flashcard_questions.a: That He is the Most Merciful, forgiving those who sincerely repent.

flashcard_questions.q: What does transcendence mean in Muslim belief about Allah?
flashcard_questions.a: That Allah is beyond and above creation, outside time and space.

flashcard_questions.q: What does immanence mean in Muslim belief about Allah?
flashcard_questions.a: That Allah is present and active within the world and people’s lives.

flashcard_questions.q: Which verse says Allah is closer to a person than their jugular vein?
Why is Adalat especially important in Shi’a Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: It is one of the Five Roots of Usul ad-Din, stressing Allah’s perfect justice.

flashcard_questions.q: What are Malaikah made from in Islamic teaching?
Why do angels always obey Allah?
flashcard_questions.a: They have no free will, unlike humans.

flashcard_questions.q: Which angel delivered the Qur’an to the Prophet Muhammad?
What is Mika’il responsible for in Islamic belief?
flashcard_questions.a: He is the angel of mercy and provision, controlling the natural world.

flashcard_questions.q: Which angel takes souls at the moment of death?

notes: 15 cards: 6 term→definition (Tawhid, Shirk, transcendence, immanence, Malaikah, Al-Qadir/Ar-Rahim), 3 belief→source (Surah 112, Surah 50:16, Al-Ikhlas), 3 angels (Jibril, Mika’il, Azra’il), 1 denomination→position (Shi’a Adalat), 1 practice→meaning (no images of God), 1 distinguishing feature (angels have no free will).
